transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yeah... I’m here because I’ve basically started planning my entire day around not using elevators. It’s getting a bit much. Like, I’m a training and development specialist, mostly teaching computer skills, right? And I had this one older student—great guy, actually. He was telling me just last week about how he used to do all his accounting on these massive paper ledgers before computers came along. My dad was an accountant too, so I remember those huge green binders taking up the whole dining room table when I was a kid, just stacks of them everywhere... 

Wait, sorry, I lost my train of thought. Right, the elevators. 

So, yeah, I’ve been taking five flights of stairs up to my apartment every single day just to avoid them. And I actually had to turn down leading a really good workshop recently because it was in this huge high-rise downtown. I even had to stop visiting that older computer student I was just talking about, because his building doesn’t really have another option besides taking the elevator up to his floor, and I just... I can't do it.
Do you feel anxious or fearful in other situations where you might feel trapped or unable to escape easily, like crowded places or being outside alone?

No, not really. Crowds are totally fine. Actually, I was just at this huge outdoor food festival last weekend and it was absolutely packed. Wall-to-wall people. They had this one food truck that did these insane Korean BBQ tacos, and I waited in line in the middle of this massive crowd for like forty-five minutes just for two of them. 

My buddy Dave was with me, and he was complaining the whole time because it was so hot out, but I kept telling him it'd be worth it. And it was, the spicy mayo they used was incredible. Dave is always complaining about something, honestly. He's the kind of guy who will get a free coffee and complain that the cup is too hot, you know? We've been friends since high school, but sometimes I just have to tune him out when he gets going on one of his rants about the weather or whatever... 

Wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Oh, right, feeling trapped. Yeah, no, being outside or in a big crowd doesn't bother me at all. It's literally just the elevators.
Do you feel anxious, panicky, or extremely uncomfortable when you're in an elevator, or when you think about getting into one?

Yeah, definitely. It's like... as soon as I even step toward one, or if I just hear those doors clunk open, my chest gets completely tight. My hands start sweating, and I get this huge rush of panic before I even have time to think about it. 

It's actually really annoying because my hands will get so sweaty that it makes it hard to use my phone. And I'm always on my phone, especially for work. We use this one app for scheduling all the training sessions, and the interface is just terrible. Like, whoever designed it clearly never had to actually use it in the real world. You have to click through like four different menus just to see your calendar for the week. I was actually thinking about emailing the developers to suggest some UI improvements, since I teach computer skills and all. I mean, it wouldn't take much to just add a shortcut button on the home screen, right? 

But anyway... yeah. The panic. It hits me immediately, like right when I hear the elevator ding.
